name: Choosing a Room Additions Contractor for Older Homes in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What should I check in a room additions contractor’s portfolio to know if they’re a good fit for older Los Angeles homes from the 1920s–1960s?
mainEntity.text: What should I check in a room additions contractor’s portfolio to know if they’re a good fit for older Los Angeles homes from the 1920s–1960s?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homes built in the 1920s–1960s in Los Angeles County often have unique architectural character and outdated systems that require special handling during a room addition. When reviewing a contractor’s portfolio, focus on projects involving homes from similar decades. Look for additions that match or thoughtfully complement original details like rooflines, stucco textures, window styles, and trim. Ask the contractor to show how they tied new foundations and framing into old systems, including solutions for uneven floors, non-standard lumber sizes, and past unpermitted work they encountered. Pay attention to how they updated electrical, plumbing, and HVAC without creating patchwork solutions or leaving parts of the home on obsolete systems. Inquire about their experience dealing with lead paint, asbestos-containing materials, and knob-and-tube wiring, which are common in older properties. Proper testing, abatement, and safe work practices are critical. The best contractor for older homes can explain how they preserve character while upgrading safety and comfort. They should be able to point to specific projects where the addition looks like it “belongs” instead of appearing bolted on. This level of experience helps protect both the aesthetics and the long-term performance of your home.
acceptedAnswer.description: For older Los Angeles homes, review a contractor’s portfolio for additions that blend with original architecture, resolve outdated wiring and plumbing, and handle lead or asbestos safely. Look for before-and-after examples on similar-age homes and ask how they tied new work into old framing and foundations.
